```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(LocusPick)
library(GenomicRanges)
ex <- locusPickExample()
td <- tempfile("LocusPick_inputs_"); dir.create(td)
```

LocusPick needs six inputs. This vignette gives several ways to produce each,
starting from the files most pipelines already write. Chunks that run on the
bundled example data are executed when the vignette is built; chunks that need
external tools (shown as `bash`) or your own files are shown but not run.

| Input | Format LocusPick reads | Required? |
|---|---|---|
| Signal tracks | bigWig, `GRanges`, chromDict, or any function | for signal ranking and plots |
| Peaks | BED / narrowPeak, `data.frame`, `GRanges` | yes |
| Gene models | GTF/GFF, or `GRanges` with `type` and `gene_name` | yes |
| DE results (×2) | any table, mapped with `deTable()` | yes |
| Expression for insets | long table: `gene`, `panel`, `group`, `value` | optional |
| Mappability | bigWig (Umap) | optional, recommended |

**Golden rule:** every input must use the **same genome build**. Run
`checkInputs()` (last section) before anything else; it catches build and
naming mismatches that otherwise fail silently.

## 1. Signal tracks (bigWig)

One bigWig per **condition** is easiest to read in figures; one per
**replicate** lets reviewers see consistency. You can make both.

### Option A: deepTools from BAM (recommended)

```bash
# per replicate; CPM-normalized, 20 bp bins, duplicates removed
bamCoverage -b young_rep1.bam -o young_rep1.bw \
    --normalizeUsing CPM --binSize 20 --ignoreDuplicates \
    --extendReads -p 8            # --extendReads: paired-end fragments

# condition mean across replicates (deepTools >= 3.5.2)
bigwigAverage -b young_rep1.bw young_rep2.bw young_rep3.bw \
    -o young_mean.bw --binSize 20 -p 8
```

Use the same normalization and bin size for every sample you will compare.
`--effectiveGenomeSize` is only needed with `--normalizeUsing RPGC`.

### Option B: from BAM in R

No command-line tools needed; uses Bioconductor packages only.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(GenomicAlignments)
bamToBigWig <- function(bam, out, paired = TRUE) {
    aln <- if (paired) granges(readGAlignmentPairs(bam), on.discordant.seqnames = "drop")
           else granges(readGAlignments(bam))
    cov <- coverage(aln) * (1e6 / length(aln))       # CPM
    rtracklayer::export(cov, out, format = "bigWig")
}
bamToBigWig("young_rep1.bam", "young_rep1.bw")
```

To average replicates in R, add coverages and divide:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
covs <- lapply(c("young_rep1.bw", "young_rep2.bw"), rtracklayer::import, as = "RleList")
rtracklayer::export(Reduce(`+`, covs) / length(covs), "young_mean.bw", format = "bigWig")
```

### Option C: from bedGraph (MACS2, SEACR, nf-core)

MACS2 writes a fragment pileup with `-B`; add `--SPMR` for signal per million
reads. SEACR and many CUT&RUN pipelines also produce bedGraphs.

```bash
macs2 callpeak -t young_rep1.bam -c igg.bam -f BAMPE -g mm \
    -n young_rep1 -B --SPMR --outdir macs2/
# -> macs2/young_rep1_treat_pileup.bdg

# bedGraph -> bigWig (UCSC tool; chrom.sizes must match your genome build)
LC_ALL=C sort -k1,1 -k2,2n young_rep1_treat_pileup.bdg > tmp.sorted.bdg
bedGraphToBigWig tmp.sorted.bdg mm10.chrom.sizes young_rep1.bw
```

Or in R (works for any bedGraph that fits in memory):

```{r}
# demo: write a bedGraph from the example track, then convert it back
bg <- file.path(td, "demo.bedGraph")
rtracklayer::export(fetchSignal(ex$signal$A, GRanges("chr1:1-60000")), bg,
                    format = "bedGraph")

gr <- rtracklayer::import(bg, format = "bedGraph")
seqlengths(gr) <- c(chr1 = 60000)          # use your genome's chrom.sizes
rtracklayer::export(gr, file.path(td, "demo.bw"), format = "bigWig")
signalAtPeaks(ex$peaks[1:2], list(demo = file.path(td, "demo.bw")))
```

A bedGraph can also be used directly, without converting, with
`rangesSource(rtracklayer::import(bg))`.

### Option D: existing chromDicts or other formats

```{r, eval = FALSE}
signal <- list(
    CNR_young = chromDictSource(readRDS("Yng.rds"), binSize = 20),
    ATAC      = functionSource(function(chr, start, end) myReader(chr, start, end)))
```

`functionSource()` accepts any function returning `start`/`end` (or `pos`) and
`score` (or `value`), so other storage formats need no conversion.

### Normalization and spike-ins

CPM/BPM assumes the total amount of binding is the same in every condition. If
a factor binds less *everywhere* in one condition, CPM hides or distorts that.
Conversely, a library-size artifact can look like global loss. For CUT&RUN
with *E. coli* or spike-in DNA, scale by the spike-in instead:

```bash
# scale = 1 / (spike-in reads in millions); compute per sample
bamCoverage -b old_rep1.bam -o old_rep1.spike.bw --binSize 20 \
    --scaleFactor 0.42 --ignoreDuplicates --extendReads
```

Whichever you choose, `signalShift()` will tell you whether a change at your
examples differs from the change at all peaks.

## 2. Peaks

### Option A: MACS2 narrowPeak / broadPeak

Read directly; rtracklayer recognizes the format by extension.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
pk <- asPeaks("macs2/young_rep1_peaks.narrowPeak")
```

### Option B: SEACR

SEACR writes `chr start end total_signal max_signal max_region`, which
`asPeaks()` reads as BED:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
pk <- asPeaks("young_rep1.stringent.bed")
```

### Option C: HOMER

Convert `peaks.txt` with HOMER's own tool, or in R:

```bash
pos2bed.pl peaks.txt > peaks.bed
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
h <- read.delim("peaks.txt", comment.char = "#", header = FALSE)
pk <- asPeaks(data.frame(chr = h$V2, start = h$V3, end = h$V4, name = h$V1))
```

If you used `annotatePeaks.pl`, keep its gene column and let LocusPick check it
(`buildCandidates(..., geneCol = "Gene.Name")`), rather than trusting it:
annotations can link enhancer peaks to genes tens of kilobases away.

### Option D: data.frame from any tool

```{r}
df <- data.frame(chr = "chr1", start = c(4799, 19799), end = c(5300, 20300))
asPeaks(df, zeroBased = TRUE)    # TRUE if the starts came from a BED file
```

### Consensus peaks across replicates

Peaks found in at least *k* replicates are more reliable examples than peaks
from a single sample.

In R:

```{r}
consensusPeaks <- function(reps, minReps = 2) {
    reps <- lapply(reps, function(x) granges(asPeaks(x)))
    merged <- reduce(do.call(c, unname(reps)))
    n <- Reduce(`+`, lapply(reps, function(r) overlapsAny(merged, r)))
    merged[n >= minReps]
}
# demo: three "replicates" made by jittering the example peaks
set.seed(1)
reps <- lapply(1:3, function(i) {
    p <- granges(ex$peaks)[sample(length(ex$peaks), 6)]
    shift(p, sample(-50:50, length(p), replace = TRUE))
})
cons <- consensusPeaks(reps, minReps = 2)
length(cons)
```

With bedtools:

```bash
cat rep1.bed rep2.bed rep3.bed | cut -f1-3 | sort -k1,1 -k2,2n \
    | bedtools merge > merged.bed
bedtools intersect -a merged.bed -b rep1.bed rep2.bed rep3.bed -c \
    | awk '$4 >= 2' | cut -f1-3 > consensus.bed
```

Condition-specific sets follow the same pattern:

```{r}
young <- cons
old   <- granges(ex$peaks)[c(1, 2, 7)]
shared     <- young[overlapsAny(young, old)]
youngOnly  <- young[!overlapsAny(young, old)]
c(shared = length(shared), youngOnly = length(youngOnly))
```

A peak-set label can be carried into the candidate table as a column:

```{r}
pk <- asPeaks(young)
pk$peak_set <- ifelse(overlapsAny(pk, old), "shared", "young-only")
```

### Blacklisted regions

Remove ENCODE blacklist regions (Amemiya et al. 2019; `mm10-blacklist.v2`,
`hg38-blacklist.v2` from the Boyle lab Blacklist repository) before ranking.
These regions give high signal in every assay and make misleading examples.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
bl <- rtracklayer::import("mm10-blacklist.v2.bed.gz")
pk <- pk[!overlapsAny(pk, bl)]
```

## 3. Gene models

### Option A: GTF from Ensembl, GENCODE or UCSC

```{r}
genes <- readGeneModels(system.file("extdata", "toy.gtf", package = "LocusPick"))
genes
```

Use the GTF that matches the genome build of your alignments: for example
GENCODE vM25 or Ensembl 102 for mm10/GRCm38. Ensembl names chromosomes `1`,
`2`, ...; UCSC and GENCODE use `chr1`. LocusPick converts between the two
automatically, but `checkInputs()` reports it so you notice.

### Option B: TxDb + OrgDb (no GTF file)

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(TxDb.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10.knownGene)
library(org.Mm.eg.db)
txdb <- TxDb.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10.knownGene
g <- GenomicFeatures::genes(txdb)
e <- unlist(GenomicFeatures::exonsBy(txdb, by = "gene"))
e$gene_id <- names(e)
sym <- AnnotationDbi::mapIds(org.Mm.eg.db, c(g$gene_id, e$gene_id),
                             "SYMBOL", "ENTREZID")
g$type <- "gene"; g$gene_name <- sym[g$gene_id]
e$type <- "exon"; e$gene_name <- sym[e$gene_id]
mcols(e) <- mcols(e)[, c("gene_id", "type", "gene_name")]
genes <- readGeneModels(c(g, e))
```

### Option C: any GRanges

`readGeneModels()` accepts a `GRanges` with a `type` column (`gene`,
`transcript` or `exon`) and a gene name column:

```{r}
gr <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(c(100, 100, 800), c(2000, 300, 2000)),
              strand = "+", type = c("gene", "exon", "exon"),
              gene_name = "myGene")
readGeneModels(gr)$genes
```

### Harmonizing symbols

If the DE tables, peak annotation and GTF come from different annotation
releases, map everything to current symbols with the same function:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
h <- function(s) harmonizeSymbols(s, org.Mm.eg.db::org.Mm.eg.db)
genes <- readGeneModels("genes.gtf", harmonize = h)
```

## 4. Differential expression tables

`defineGroups()` needs two tables: the **perturbation** (e.g. knockout vs
control) and the **condition** (e.g. old vs young). `deTable()` maps any
column names to `gene`, `lfc`, `padj`.

> **Check the direction of every contrast.** Fold changes must be
> *perturbation / control* and *condition / baseline* (e.g. KO / WT,
> old / young). A reversed contrast swaps activated and repressed targets
> without any error.

### Option A: DESeq2

```{r, eval = FALSE}
res <- DESeq2::results(dds, contrast = c("genotype", "KO", "WT"))   # KO / WT
df <- as.data.frame(res)
df$gene <- rownames(df)
ko <- deTable(df, gene = "gene", lfc = "log2FoldChange", padj = "padj")
```

The same mapping applies to a DESeq2 table saved to disk:

```{r}
deseq <- data.frame(row.names = c("geneA", "geneB", "geneC"),
                    baseMean = c(200, 50, 120), log2FoldChange = c(-2, 1.5, -1),
                    lfcSE = 0.2, pvalue = c(1e-8, 1e-6, 1e-4),
                    padj = c(1e-6, 1e-5, 1e-3))
deseq$gene <- rownames(deseq)
deTable(deseq, gene = "gene", lfc = "log2FoldChange", padj = "padj")
```

### Option B: edgeR

```{r, eval = FALSE}
tt <- edgeR::topTags(qlf, n = Inf)$table
tt$gene <- rownames(tt)
ko <- deTable(tt, gene = "gene", lfc = "logFC", padj = "FDR")
```

### Option C: limma / limma-voom

```{r, eval = FALSE}
tt <- limma::topTable(fit, coef = "genotypeKO", number = Inf)
tt$gene <- rownames(tt)
ko <- deTable(tt, gene = "gene", lfc = "logFC", padj = "adj.P.Val")
```

### Ensembl IDs instead of symbols

Strip version suffixes, then map to symbols:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
ids <- sub("\\.\\d+$", "", rownames(df))          # ENSMUSG00000017950.16 -> ...950
df$gene <- AnnotationDbi::mapIds(org.Mm.eg.db::org.Mm.eg.db, ids,
                                 "SYMBOL", "ENSEMBL")
df <- df[!is.na(df$gene), ]
```

`deTable()` keeps the most significant row when several IDs map to one symbol.

### Restricting to bound genes

To restrict groups to genes with a peak (as "direct targets"), pass them as
`targets`:

```{r}
bound <- unique(assignPeaks(ex$peaks, ex$genes)$gene)
de <- read.delim(system.file("extdata", "toy_de.tsv", package = "LocusPick"))
defineGroups(deTable(de, lfc = "ko_lfc", padj = "ko_padj"),
             deTable(de, lfc = "cond_lfc", padj = "cond_padj"),
             targets = bound, conditionName = "age")[, c("gene", "group")]
```

## 5. Expression for insets

`plotLocus()` draws expression from a long table with one row per sample:
`gene`, `panel` (one facet per experiment), `group`, `value`.

### Option A: from a matrix and sample sheet

Works for DESeq2 normalized counts, TPM, or any gene × sample matrix:

```{r}
toLong <- function(mat, groups, panel) {
    data.frame(gene  = rep(rownames(mat), times = ncol(mat)),
               panel = panel,
               group = rep(groups, each = nrow(mat)),
               value = as.vector(mat))
}
# demo matrix: 3 genes x 6 samples
mat <- matrix(rpois(18, 100), nrow = 3,
              dimnames = list(c("geneA", "geneB", "geneC"), paste0("s", 1:6)))
long <- toLong(mat, groups = rep(c("Young", "Old"), each = 3), panel = "Aging")
head(long)
```

With DESeq2:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
mat <- DESeq2::counts(dds, normalized = TRUE)
long <- toLong(mat, groups = as.character(dds$age), panel = "Aging")
```

### Option B: combine several experiments

```{r, eval = FALSE}
expression <- rbind(
    toLong(koCounts,  koSamples$genotype, panel = "Hnf4a KO"),
    toLong(ageCounts, ageSamples$age,     panel = "Aging"))
expression$gene <- h(expression$gene)    # same symbol harmonization as above
```

Groups are drawn in the order they first appear, so order the rows (or the
sample sheet) control-first.

## 6. Mappability

### Option A: Umap multi-read mappability (recommended)

Umap (Karimzadeh et al. 2018) provides, for each base, the fraction of
overlapping k-mers that map uniquely. The authors distribute mm9, mm10, hg19
and hg38 as bedGraphs; the bundled script converts one to a bigWig once:

```{r}
system.file("scripts", "make_umap_bw.sh", package = "LocusPick")
```

```bash
bash make_umap_bw.sh 50     # k: closest to your read length (24, 36, 50, 100)
```

Run it on a node with ~16 GB memory; the intermediate bedGraph is several GB.

### Option B: blacklist only

If you cannot use Umap, remove blacklisted regions from the peaks (section 2)
and leave `mappability = NULL`. This removes the worst regions but not
paralog clusters.

### Option C: build Umap for another genome

The Umap software (`bioconda::umap`) computes mappability for any genome; see
its documentation. It needs substantial compute (the authors report about 200
CPU hours per read length).

## 7. Check everything together

```{r}
checkInputs(ex$peaks, ex$genes, signal = ex$signal, groups = ex$groups)
```

The warning is expected here: the example data deliberately contain one peak in
a gap of the signal tracks. On real data, a handful of such peaks is normal;
a large fraction points to a different genome build or chromosome naming in
the track.

A common failure, gene models from a different build than the peaks, looks
like this:

```{r}
shifted <- shift(ex$genes$genes, 1e6)   # simulate gene models from another build
bad <- ex$genes; bad$genes <- shifted
checkInputs(ex$peaks, bad)
```

## Suggested end-to-end workflow

```bash
# 1. signal: one bigWig per replicate and per condition
for s in young_rep{1..3} old_rep{1..3}; do
  bamCoverage -b $s.bam -o $s.bw --normalizeUsing CPM --binSize 20 \
      --ignoreDuplicates --extendReads -p 8
done
bigwigAverage -b young_rep*.bw -o young.bw --binSize 20
bigwigAverage -b old_rep*.bw   -o old.bw   --binSize 20

# 2. mappability (once per genome and read length)
bash make_umap_bw.sh 50
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(LocusPick)
h <- function(s) harmonizeSymbols(s, org.Mm.eg.db::org.Mm.eg.db)

# 3. gene models and peaks
genes <- readGeneModels("gencode.vM25.annotation.gtf", harmonize = h)
bl    <- rtracklayer::import("mm10-blacklist.v2.bed.gz")
peaks <- consensusPeaks(list("young_rep1_peaks.narrowPeak",
                             "young_rep2_peaks.narrowPeak",
                             "young_rep3_peaks.narrowPeak"), minReps = 2)
peaks <- asPeaks(peaks[!overlapsAny(peaks, bl)])

# 4. groups (check contrast directions!)
ko  <- deTable(read.csv("ko_vs_wt_deseq2.csv"),   gene = "gene",
               lfc = "log2FoldChange", padj = "padj")
age <- deTable(read.csv("old_vs_young_deseq2.csv"), gene = "gene",
               lfc = "log2FoldChange", padj = "padj")
ko$gene <- h(ko$gene); age$gene <- h(age$gene)
groups <- defineGroups(ko, age, conditionName = "age")

# 5. check, then build
signal <- list(young = "young.bw", old = "old.bw")
checkInputs(peaks, genes, signal, groups)
cand <- buildCandidates(peaks, genes, groups, signal = signal,
                        mappability = "k50.Umap.MultiTrackMappability.bw")
```

Continue with `rankLoci()` as described in `vignette("LocusPick")`.
